narr: Two voices, on purpose. The president's: Pezeshkian told the General Assembly on Wednesday that Iran will 'never bow our head, or bend the knee' and is 'ready for dialogue and diplomacy without accepting the language of force', held up the photographs of the assassinated Leader and the Minab schoolgirls, and called the United States 'the victims' maker of terrorists' — the US and Israeli delegations walked out. The soldiers': Safavi, the Leader's military adviser, said any force 'attempting to land in Iran will certainly be destroyed', that Iran's radars follow US warships from the Gulf to the Indian Ocean, and that the strait reopens only when the blockade lifts and Iran's terms are met — Oman, he says, has a mechanism and Washington 'obstructs' it; the Armed Forces promised a reply 'more severe than previous'; Abdollahi: 'no security for aggressors'. Underneath both, the channel is real for the first time since Islamabad: Baghaei confirms 'another round of message exchange and clarification ... through the Qatari mediator' in New York on Tuesday — two hours by his count, three by Trump's, with Witkoff and Kushner across the table — and lists four conditions 'conveyed ... in a manner that leaves no doubt or ambiguity': end the blockade and the 'aggressive actions', end the war on all fronts, release the blocked assets, recognise the Iran–Oman corridor. Rezaei says the same terms went to Qatar and Pakistan; Fars called the Reuters/Kyodo 'reopen in seven days' report 'unreliable and inaccurate'. Nobody in Tehran has claimed the Cape Dao (Sep 23, one Indian seafarer killed) or the LR Stephanie/Al Maryah pair (Sep 21); Al Mayadeen's index, still behind Cloudflare, carries 'IRGC targets 2 ships near Hormuz after repeat US violations' (undated) beside 'Strait of Hormuz closed until Trump, Netanyahu, removed' and 'Iran denies US crossed Hormuz, calls claims fabricated' — the framing is that the strait is Iran's to close and no US convoy has passed. The airline shutdown took effect Wednesday (flights to Turkey, the UAE and China cancelled; Oman, Azerbaijan and Georgia closed their skies); the rial answered at 234,900, weaker by 4,400 in three days. The NPT bill is still paper. ADDENDUM, Thursday 07:00 daily: the soldiers spoke again before Xi sat down — Safavi (Press TV, 09:33 GMT) said new US or Israeli attacks would take the war 'beyond the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz', that Iran keeps control of the strait, and that Chinese vessels may pass; Pezeshkian told Europe to rethink its snapback line; an IRGC official told Al Mayadeen on Tuesday that 'the war is still ongoing, the strait is not open and the US is lying'. At home, the IRGC announced that Brig Gen Hossein Zarifi, head of the Shahid Sajjad base, was killed in an operation at Saravan on Wednesday — no adversary named. Nobody in Tehran has claimed the six missiles at Yanbu and Taif; nobody has confirmed a second round in New York. The rial firmed by 200 to 234,700. ADDENDUM, Thursday 11:00: Tehran put its price in public and its hand in private on the same afternoon. In public, Rezaei (IRIB): seven conditions, the Americans have four to five days, and 'neither the Strait of Hormuz will be opened nor negotiations begin' before they are met; the IRGC's Vahidi and the army's Hatami echoed the president's 'we do not fear war'. In private, by Reuters' count of six sources, a senior Iranian official sketched the phased way out — 'the first [stage] would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz' — and regional sources say the transit-fee demand can go into a side attachment because the blockade hurts more than the toll is worth; the same official: 'our fingers are on the trigger'. The Houthis claimed 'dozens' of missiles and drones on Saudi positions at al-Tuwal and al-Daghareer in Jizan (no Saudi confirmation); Moscow's Ulyanov said IAEA inspectors cannot return while Washington threatens daily. The rial firmed to 234,200. Al Mayadeen was not reached (Cloudflare) — no new carry since Tuesday's 'the strait is not open'. ADDENDUM, Thursday 15:00: Tehran claimed its hit and sharpened its threat. The IRGC posted video of the cargo ship burning in the strait — 'at least one projectile struck the violating vessel' — which is the first claim of responsibility for the Cape Dao, the sixty-second UKMTO report and the first death at sea since the El Gaia. By evening the IRGC's Intelligence Unit put every US asset 'on land and water, including US warships' under 'the threat of continuous and sustained strikes' and claimed the Americans are dispersing to Jordan and going underground — intent, not fire. Ghalibaf mocked the ten-year at 5.1% ('the floor two years out … bell-bottoms'); Araghchi asked Europe to 'confront US aggression'; Kata'ib Hezbollah asked Iraqis to break the 'siege'. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Thursday 19:00: Tehran put a clock on the table and widened its threat. Araghchi told reporters in New York that Iran handed the mediators a seven-day plan this week — meet the conditions and the strait opens on the seventh day, then talks toward a final deal; Pezeshkian said out loud that Iran wants the Americans 'back in the MoU before the midterms'. The same evening the deputy foreign minister told Europe its bases 'will not go unanswered', and the Indian seamen's union said the Cape Dao took two torpedoes. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Thursday 23:00: by dawn in the Gulf Tehran had hardened its public line without touching the channel. Rezaei: until the conditions are met the strait stays shut 'and we will not negotiate'; an Iranian source called the New York contacts 'workshops to explore positions'; Pezeshkian told Fox that America 'must choose', and that the Houthis answer for themselves. The IRGC's intelligence arm claimed the Americans had been forced to disperse and dig in. Reuters, meanwhile, had six sources on a phased sequence — blockade off, strait open, then the rest — and Tehran ready to park its transit fee. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Friday 03:00: Tehran's spokesman put the New York contact on the record — Qatar-mediated, Iran's conditions conveyed 'very clearly': fighting ends on all fronts, the blockade and the economic war stop, the assets come back. Ghalibaf told parliament the enemy had been 'taught a valuable lesson'; Mehr counted 313,000 at a national-defence rally; a lawmaker said there would be no Pezeshkian–Trump meeting. The squeeze on Iran's airlines reached Najaf, where Iraq halted every Iranian flight at 23:00 GMT — the first neighbour to act since Rezaei's warning. The rial firmed a shade to 233,900. ADDENDUM, Friday 07:00: Araghchi gave the paper a shape — seven days: guns silent on every front including Lebanon, the blockade and the oil sanctions lifted, the assets released, the strait open at the end of the seventh day, the nuclear file after; 'the moment they accept this plan … this timetable can start'. Rezaei's 'not until the conditions are met' and the president's 'America must choose' framed it; Qatar's prime minister hosted Pezeshkian on de-escalation. Araghchi told Lavrov the US had reneged on the Islamabad understanding and briefed him on the Oman shipping lanes. The airline squeeze reached all four Iraqi airports, and the Leader's adviser answered that regional flights would be 'open to everyone or to no one'. The rial firmed to 233,600. ADDENDUM, Friday 11:00: Tehran worked the Arab side of the table. Araghchi sat with Saudi Arabia's Faisal bin Farhan in New York — IRIB's footage, no Saudi readout yet — after Egypt's Abdelatty took up 'proposals being put forward', and Pakistan's Sharif told the Assembly that Islamabad's mediation goes on. At home the aviation authority stopped selling tickets to Iraq once all four Iraqi airports had shut Iranian carriers out, giving Mokhber's 'everyone or no one' a first, bloodless act. The army's voice was technical: capabilities 'reconfigured', the Arash drone upgraded, cheap missiles to drain the enemy's magazines. Nothing was fired at sea or at the Americans; two US tankers flew over the UAE unmolested. The rial held at 233,600. ADDENDUM, Friday 15:00: Tehran put a clock on the table. Araghchi, to reporters at the UN: the seven days start 'as soon as the United States accepts this plan' — 'if they accept this plan tomorrow, the seven days will start from tomorrow'; the American steps are 'all already in the MoU' and could be done in four or five days; the strait opens on day six, the talks resume on day seven; 'the choice now rests with the United States'. The National's sources say the roadmap carries a term he did not say aloud: dilute the 60% stockpile, then send it out under IAEA mechanisms — and a warning that if nothing comes by the end of the period, military operations could resume. Rezaei kept the other hand up: 'until our conditions are met, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened'. The IRGC's spokesman called Iran the victor and the strait a proof that Washington cannot keep it open 'for even a few hours'. Velayati told Iraq's prime minister that legitimacy comes 'from the soil of Najaf'. Pezeshkian thanked Xi; Miliband came to Araghchi's table. The rial slipped a hundred to 233,700. Nothing was fired. ADDENDUM, Friday 19:00: Tehran spent the night on the nuclear file and the Iraqi front. Guterres told Pezeshkian, by Tehran's telling, that he does not think Iran is seeking a bomb; Pezeshkian told Fox's Bret Baier that Iran could lower enrichment and let outsiders verify it as a first step, and that the Leader holds the bomb 'unholy'; the Majlis committee chairman Jokar answered from Tehran that 60% stays — 'exactly what the enemies want'. The IRGC's spokesman called Iran the victor. Across the border, Iraq cut ground services to Iranian airlines at three airports under the US sanctions threat, and the militias answered: Nujaba wants sit-ins at the airports, Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada wants parliament to say 'no to the blockade'. The rial did not move. The strait did not either: Sep 25 closed at 3 in and 10 out, not a barrel on the export counter. ADDENDUM, Friday 23:00: Tehran offered and threatened in the same night. Araghchi sat with Oman's Albusaidi in New York and the two readouts spoke of 'safe navigation', 'freedom of passage' and 'a safe maritime route' — the Oman route thread's first dated move in ten days. The president told CBS that UN inspectors could come back, 'absolutely', through negotiation, and that the bomb is 'haram'. And in the same hours a senior official told Reuters there would be no concessions on enrichment or on shipping the 60% stock out, and that the strait stays shut until every condition is met; the IRGC's spokesman said Iran 'will not stop punishing the United States'. The rial slipped 100 to 233,600. The strait's log at dawn: one in, five out. ADDENDUM, Saturday 03:00: the president spoke to Al Jazeera on his way out of New York. 'We no longer trust talks with Washington', he said — 'repeated attacks and sanctions following every negotiation' — but Qatar and Pakistan are carrying the messages, the talks rest on the June memorandum and 'the Americans must state their position on it'; the strait 'will remain open for trade if negotiations lead to resolving the dispute'. He thanked Xi on X for backing a return to the Islamabad MoU. Then the operational command spoke: Khatam al-Anbiya HQ, via Mehr, said all US 'deployment centres and interests in the region will be targeted if Washington makes a mistake' — 'Iran will not start the war'. The rial opened the week at 235,200, up 1,600. ADDENDUM, Saturday 07:00: before Washington's word came, the president put the plan under the leader's name — to CBS (IRNA excerpts) it was 'coordinated with the leader of the revolution' and Iran 'would fulfil its obligations' the day the US accepts; Press TV's headline: ready for talks, no 'bullying and coercion'. The Defence Ministry said part of the army's strategic capacity is now underground; the security council said Rezaei's airport threat had been 'inaccurately interpreted' — no military retaliation over the airline bans, the talks to lift them 'pursued seriously'. The central bank found a number to like: inflation 83.8%, the first dip in fifteen months. The rial gave back 400. ADDENDUM, Saturday 11:00: Tehran heard the rejection on camera and answered with distrust and a channel in the same breath. Pezeshkian, to Al Jazeera (aired Saturday): 'we have no trust in the American side and do not know on what basis an understanding can be reached with it' — and yet Qatar and Pakistan carry the messages, the talks rest on the June memorandum, and Washington 'must make clear its stance' on it; to CBS, taped Friday for Sunday: '440 kilograms of 60 percent enriched uranium', inspections 'within the negotiations', the route 'was supposed to be determined between Iran and Oman'. The soldiers' voice was Shekarchi's: '100 per cent readiness', a 'heavier and broader response' to any new attack. Araghchi called the sanctions 'economic terrorism' and stays in New York until Wednesday. Nothing was fired. The rial gave back another 300. ADDENDUM, Saturday 15:00: Tehran's answer to the public 'no' is patience with conditions attached. Araghchi, to Reuters around 21:30 GMT: Tehran 'has seen' the president's reaction but waits for the 'definitive US position' to come through the mediators, and will decide on that — 'our conditions are clear, and any move towards reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met'; 'only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock'. Pezeshkian landed in Tehran and said the Assembly had been 'an opportunity to state that those who violate international law and talk about trust are the most destructive and untrustworthy in the world'; IRNA listed his meetings — Iraq, Lebanon, Pakistan, the Netherlands, Norway, Switzerland, Armenia, Bangladesh, Guterres, Costa. Gharibabadi chose the disarmament day to ask 'how can we speak of disarmament while ignoring the nuclear arsenal of the Zionist regime'. The Houthi military counted twenty-seven Saudi airstrikes in a day and fired nothing new at the kingdom. The rial took back 200. ADDENDUM, Saturday 19:00: Tehran put the wait in writing and sharpened the threat around it. Araghchi's Telegram statement (01:30 GMT Sunday): New York was for stating the Supreme National Security Council's conditions; the mediators carried them; 'we have seen the first reaction from the US president, but nothing has been conveyed to us from the mediators yet'; the president's 'contradictory statements' mean Tehran waits for 'the definitive opinions' and 'will make a decision based on that'; reopening 'is contingent on the fulfilment of Iran's conditions — we will not back down from them'; 'no one in the world' can accuse Iran of not trying diplomacy. Pezeshkian told Al Jazeera Iran 'no longer trusts' the talks — every round followed by attacks and sanctions — while Qatar and Pakistan relay the messages. The soldiers' voice was Shekarchi's again: the Americans 'dream of interfering in the Strait of Hormuz, and if they interfere … they will be slapped' (Tasnim, 22:40 GMT), and on Sunday 'surprises in store', 'new military technologies', missiles and drones 'more advanced and more powerful'. The strait's paperwork spoke too: the Persian Gulf Strait Authority warned owners that charterers 'forcing vessels to transit through invalid routes' risk 'financial and human losses' and a Non-Compliance listing. Iran said it would not answer the airline sanctions militarily. The rial did not move. ADDENDUM, Saturday 23:00: the navy's voice joined the soldiers'. IRGC Navy deputy Ali Mohammadi (Fars, overnight): 'if another war breaks out, we will undoubtedly attack and hit their ships and destroyers even in the Indian Ocean' — and Washington's 'control' of the strait is not what the sea shows. Araghchi, on camera at dawn Tehran time, said the same thing he wrote on Telegram: the answer has to come through the mediators, none has, Iran waits. Three top-command threats in twelve hours; no act at sea in four days; the rial eased 200 to 234,500. ADDENDUM, Sunday 03:00: the army chief spoke at a ceremony on Sunday morning — 'the war is not over; we have won, but we must consolidate this victory' — and, per Al Jazeera's reading of it, told the neighbours the strait stays shut until Washington's economic war ends. His spokesman said the Americans, in a 'precarious' position, may attack again. From the Majlis a deputy speaker wanted the energy door shut to everyone or to no one. Araghchi, on X, kept the other line open: 'only a negotiated solution', and Iran waits for the mediators' 'definitive views'. Pezeshkian said Tehran no longer trusts the American side. The rial, on its first working-day print since the rejection, gave up 1,300 to 235,800. ADDENDUM, Sunday 07:00: at midday Tehran the Guards' navy said it had taken a second American robot from the water — 'an advanced submersible called Remus 600', caught 'in a coordinated and complex operation with intelligence and electronic warfare', its memory now with the specialists — and restated, in the same breath, that 'the Strait of Hormuz is closed'. The army chief's morning speech was fuller than the first summary: 'the strait of our honour'; 'if Iran can't live, no one can trade and live'; to the neighbours, that cooperation with Washington 'does not create security' and that the Americans' removal from the region 'is not far away'. The IRGC Navy's deputy promised, if war resumes, to strike American 'vessels and destroyers, even in the Indian Ocean'. Araghchi, on X, listed the conditions once more — a halt to hostilities everywhere, Lebanon included — and said Tehran waits for the mediators' 'definitive positions'. The rial slid to 236,100. ADDENDUM, Sunday 11:00: the morning's drone claim did not survive the afternoon — CENTCOM told Al Jazeera it has 'positive control' of every operational drone and called the story 'clearly desperate'. Tehran's answer was more voices, not evidence: the Leader's adviser Safavi said the Americans 'are on their way out' and called the strait 'a very important lever'; the army's spokesman promised a 'more forceful, extensive and decisive' answer to any new attack; the deputy foreign minister told the Treasury the world is not its 'backyard'. Araghchi, on American television, held both doors open at once — 'even if it comes to a doomsday war' and 'diplomacy can never fail' — and said Iran still waits for an official answer through the mediators. The rial eased to 235,600 by evening.
